shortDescription: Resolve a GitHub release to a downloadable, verifiable artefact.

options.name: architecture
options.description: Target CPU architecture used to select the artefact, typically taken from C(ansible_facts.architecture). Synonyms are handled automatically (for example C(x86_64)/C(amd64), C(aarch64)/C(arm64)).

options.name: asset
options.description: Explicit artefact filename template overriding the heuristic. Supported placeholders: C({version}) (without leading C(v)), C({tag}) (raw tag), C({system}) (lowercased) and C({arch}) (raw architecture). Mutually exclusive with O(asset_regex).

options.name: asset_regex
options.description: Regular expression matched against asset names, overriding the heuristic. Mutually exclusive with O(asset).

options.name: cache
options.description: Validity of cached release metadata in minutes. Prevents unnecessary repeated GitHub API calls.

options.name: exclude_keywords
options.description: Keywords excluded when resolving O(version=latest). A release whose name or tag contains any keyword (case-insensitive) is skipped.

options.name: extensions
options.description: Ordered archive extension preference used to disambiguate multiple matching artefacts. The first extension with a match wins.

options.name: password
options.description: Optional GitHub personal access token. Raises the API rate limit and enables access to private repositories.

options.name: project
options.description: Defines the project (owner or organisation) in which the repository was created. For example: B(prometheus)/alertmanager

options.name: repository
options.description: Defines the repository maintained underneath the given project. For example: prometheus/B(alertmanager)

options.name: system
options.description: Target operating system used to select the artefact, typically taken from C(ansible_facts.system).

options.name: user
options.description: Optional GitHub username (currently informational; authentication uses the token supplied via O(password)).

options.name: version
options.description: Requested version. Use V(latest) to resolve the highest non-excluded SemVer release, or a concrete version with or without a leading C(v) (for example V(2.53.0) or V(v2.53.0)).
